_comment: Manually authored per-image, per-variant layout. Every crop and text position here was chosen by gridding/cropping that specific photo and measuring its actual negative space and product/model boundaries — nothing is computed by the renderer. `crop` is {x,y,width,height} in the ORIGINAL MASTER's pixel coordinates (a lossless sharp .extract(), never a resize/distort — width/height are always exactly 4:5). All other coordinates (textBox, supportPosition, dividerPosition, brandPosition) are in the CROPPED canvas's own coordinates (top-left of the crop = 0,0), since that crop is the actual output canvas. A variant may set headlineLinesOverride/accentLineIndexOverride to test a different line-break of the SAME assigned copy from copy.json (not different words).

MOL_IMG_001._photo_notes: REVISED round 2: round-1 variants kept the crop's right edge at the original x1122 the whole time because the product's right boundary was mismeasured (assumed ~x1090-1100). Re-measured precisely this round: the socks actually end at x~1005. That freed ~85-90px of previously-unused margin on the right — this round's 'product still too small' fix comes from trimming the crop's right edge down to x1035-1090 (25-55px of real margin past the sock, not 120px of empty rug/table it had before). Text zone is the same out-of-focus curtain strip at top-right, now measured against each variant's own (tighter) right edge, which is why headline size shrinks a bit as the crop tightens (V1 69px -> V3 56px): trading zone width for product prominence, which is what was asked for.

MOL_IMG_005._photo_notes: REVISED round 5 — same photo, same crop, headline re-broken to 4 lines ('Self-care'/'doesn't'/'need a'/'timeout.') and every element re-measured against a full pixel-grid pass of the master (not eyeballed), because round 4's request to move the whole composition to the 'upper-left clean wall' turned out not to be physically possible: an objective largest-clean-rectangle scan (color-distance from confirmed wall pixels) of x0-650,y0-650 found the biggest pocket clearing the picture frame, potted plant, jar shelf, utensil canister/cutting boards/lemon bowl, and the model's head/hair is either ~391x51px or ~140x71px — neither tall enough for a 4-line headline at any legible size. The only run in this whole photo with both enough width and height is the lower cabinet-front strip used in rounds 3-4, confirmed with the user before proceeding. Within that strip: the model's hip/pants/leg edge is NOT confined to the y700-730 pinch (~x360) as previously documented — it runs continuously down the whole crop, sitting at roughly x360-400 all the way from y~630 to past y1190 (it's her leg, not just her hip), which the first render of this round missed and produced a support line overlapping her pants. Headline: the 4 shorter lines are each individually narrower than round 4's 'doesn't need', so the same ~x355 right-edge budget now allows a much bigger 72px font (up from 51px), widest line 'Self-care' at 280.5px, ~25px clear of the leg. Support: at the required 28px-minimum, 'Wear MOLOSOC while life keeps moving.' measures 546.8px as one line — far too wide to fit left of her leg at any y — so it's wrapped (supportLinesOverride, same rule as headline overrides: reconstructs the exact copy.json sentence, never different words) to 'Wear MOLOSOC' / 'while life' / 'keeps moving.', widest line only 223.3px, comfortably clear. The dark shadowed toe-kick recess under the cabinet (~y1000-1060, RGB brightness ~30-65) sits right where this 3-line support block now starts, but there's no cleaner alternative band before the rug (~y1150) and the actual MOLOSOC socks (confirmed by precise crop: ankle visible from ~y1190, white sock fabric from ~y1230-1250) — the whole support/divider/brand block ends at y1190.4, still 40+px clear of the socks. REVISED round 6: whole block nudged up (headline top 630->615, clear of the lemon bowl which was re-checked and only reaches down to ~y590) and every size stepped up slightly — headline 72->74, support 28->32, wordmark 24->27 — spacing between elements kept the same proportions. Re-verified: widest headline line 'Self-care' at 74px is 288.3px, still ~17px clear of the leg edge; support/divider/brand (now ending y~1201) still ~30px clear of the socks (~y1230).

MOL_IMG_019._photo_notes: Approved as-is this round — unchanged from the prior round. Standing, watering plants. Head ~y40, product (socks) ~x530-870,y1150-1300. Crop trims only the right side (chair/window); the large plain-wall zone top-left (x55-485,y55+) is untouched by the trim, so text layout is identical across variants — the variation here is purely crop tightness/product prominence.

MOL_IMG_012._photo_notes: Standing/kitchen preview (next-3 batch). Full master used as canvas (no crop). Her sleeve/leg sits at a fairly consistent x~300-320 from y340 (arm) down through y700-1100+ (leg), so the left cabinet strip is narrower here than MOL_IMG_005's — textBox width capped at 260 (right edge 315, ~15-25px clear of x300-320) rather than 005's 300, which is why the headline (40px) is smaller than 005's 74px: this photo's own negative space, not a fixed template size. Support wraps 3 ways (same supportLinesOverride mechanism as 005) since the one-line sentence at 28px (442px) is far too wide for this narrower zone.

V2._variant_note: Option A: same 3-line break as V1, headline held at the same safe 40px (her sleeve's soft edge sits ~x285-300 here throughout y370-750 — confirmed against the actual V1 render, not just the photo grid — so 'complicated.' at 40px/230.7px-wide, right edge 285.7, is this zone's real ceiling without risking overlap). What changes is spacing: headlineLineHeight 1.15->1.35 for real breathing room between lines, support/wordmark stepped up (28->30 / 22->24) for clearer hierarchy, and the whole block starts higher (y400->370, right under the shelf) with wider gaps between headline/support/divider/brand so it reads as one deliberate, resolved block instead of a cramped one.

V3._variant_note: Option B: literally stacks the headline across 4 lines ('Simple'/'care.'/'Nothing'/'complicated.') instead of 3, per the 'stack across more lines to make it larger and cleaner' instruction. The width ceiling is unchanged (still bounded by 'complicated.' at 40px, same 285.7px right edge as V1/V2 — no single line was ever wider than that word), but 4 short, generously-spaced lines (lineHeight 1.3) occupy more vertical presence and read as a bolder, more editorial stack than 3 denser lines.

V4._variant_note: Option C: same 3-line headline as V1/V2 at the same safe 40px, but the whole four-part block (headline/support/divider/brand, total height ~366px) is vertically centered within the full clean cabinet run (shelf ends ~y340, her leg/counter don't force a stop until ~y950) rather than pinned right under the shelf — equal breathing room above and below so the block feels deliberately placed in the middle of the negative space, not just dropped at its top edge.

MOL_IMG_018._photo_notes: Relaxed/sofa preview (next-3 batch). Full master used as canvas (no crop). The whole upper-left is clean sheer curtain, but a narrow column (x55-150) stays clean far deeper (past y500) than the wider block does (her hair reaches x180-250 by y390-420) — so the whole 4-part stack (headline/support/divider/brand) is kept inside the fully-clean band above y~380 rather than risking the diagonal hairline, which keeps every size more compact than MOL_IMG_005's: headline 58px, support 20px wrapped 3 ways, wordmark 16px.

MOL_IMG_020._photo_notes: Seated/floor preview (next-3 batch). Full master used as canvas (no crop). Same diagonal-hairline shape as MOL_IMG_018 (she's seated against the sofa, leaning her head down/right onto the book) — headline (60px) fits in the fully-clean band above y~260, but the support line ('Make it part of the moments you already enjoy.' — the longest supporting line of any post so far) would need ~245px+ at any comfortable size, which crosses into her hairline once positioned below the headline. Wrapped into 4 short lines at 22px (widest 144.5px) to stay inside the narrow x55-200 column that stays clean to y~400.

MOL_IMG_002._photo_notes: REVISED again — one rigid 3-line block now (no headlineLineGaps, no per-line repositioning), per the locked-headline rule. Solved by finding a single Y where the WHOLE block's real ink span (which runs from Y-29 to Y+399 at 135px/0.90 — the font's true ascent/descent extends well beyond the nominal line box) clears every obstacle at once: her chin (~y400-410), her hand (~x580-720,y950-1050), and the sock (~x150-350,y900-1000). Y=445 puts the block's ink at 415.8-844.9 — 5px clear of her chin above and, more importantly, ~55px clear of the sock/hand below. Support/divider/brand keep tight but real gaps (12/8/8px) to land at y821.5-895.9, ~4px clear of the sock — the tightest safe margin in this batch, but a real one, not an estimate.

MOL_IMG_003._photo_notes: REVISED again — one rigid 3-line block, per the locked-headline rule. Her face runs to the very top of frame (chin ~y300) and she holds an open book with both hands at ~x600-780,y480-620; the block's own ink span at Y=310 runs 280.8-708.9 — clears her chin (5-15px) and clears her hands by ~19px (line 1's descender reaches only to ~471, well short of 480). The other two lines are narrow enough ('A little' / 'quiet.') that they don't reach her hands' x-range at all regardless of y. Her feet/sock are further right (~x650+) and never enter this block's horizontal reach. Support/divider/brand follow with normal spacing at y710+, more than 200px clear of the sock (~y960+).

MOL_IMG_004._photo_notes: FLAGGED CONFLICT — could not fully satisfy the locked single-rigid-block rule and 'never cover hands' simultaneously for this photo; explaining why rather than silently picking one. Her obstacles stack too densely for a rigid 428px-tall ink block (3 lines at 135px/0.90) to dodge all of them: chin ends ~y260, she's gripping the vacuum with one hand on the canister (~x330-420,y490-570) and one on the handle (~x480-560,y620-720), and her socks start ~y1090. The two hand-free gaps this could sit in are the chin-to-hand gap (260-490, only 230px) and the hand-to-sock gap (720-1090, 370px) — both smaller than the 428px block needs, so no single Y clears the chin, both hands, AND the sock at once. This lays the block at Y=300 (ink 270.8-698.9): it clears her chin (10px) and clears the sock by ~390px, prioritizing the two rules that have mattered most across this whole project (face, then product) — but its own ink does cross both hand grips, which the old per-line-gap version had avoided by routing around them individually. Flagging this rather than either silently shipping the hand overlap or unilaterally overriding the new one-block rule to fix it.

MOL_IMG_006._photo_notes: REVISED again — one rigid 3-line block for the headline itself fits, but flagging a related conflict for the secondary lockup below it. Still shifted to x=160 (sharp-focus framed print at x0-145). Her chin ends ~y300, her hands are on the laptop/desk at ~x550-720,y560-680, and — measured precisely this round, tighter than earlier estimated — her sock starts at ~y1120, not ~y1150. The only gap big enough for the 428px headline block is between her hands and the sock (680-1120, 440px), and it barely fits: Y=715 puts the block's ink at 685.8-1113.9, ~6px clear on both sides. But that leaves only ~40px between the headline and the sock for support+divider+brand to fit 'underneath the headline' as required — physically less than support+divider+brand need even with zero spacing (~58px). Divider (90px wide) is narrow enough it never reaches the sock's x-range, but support and brand do, and can't both be squeezed above y1120: this lockup unavoidably overlaps the top few px of the sock at whatever position it takes. Flagging rather than silently shipping it or unilaterally resizing/detaching the lockup to dodge it.

MOL_IMG_007._photo_notes: REVISED again — same 135px/0.90 typography and same position as the previous round (kept per 'close to current look'): this was already the best-behaved of the five, with line 3 clearing her entirely and only a ~10px graze of the left edge of her hair from line 2 ('Your feet') — a soft hair edge, not her face/hairline proper, so left as-is.
